💡 This work pioneers an isoreticular redox-core tailoring strategy to create complementary n-type and p-type COFs from related architectures. By pairing triazine and triphenylamine cores, it achieves a rare high-voltage all-COF sodium dual-ion battery (3.40 V average, 116 mAh g⁻¹, 76 mAh g⁻¹ after 1000 cycles), establishing molecular design principles for regulating electrochemical function in crystalline organic frameworks.

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Superlattice engineering of relaxor ferroelectric BZT-BCT with paraelectric SrTiO₃ yields a lead-free capacitor achieving ~99% efficiency and 12.6 J/cm³ recoverable energy density at 920 kV/cm. Novelty lies in combining polar nanoregion confinement with strain-gradient-modified built-in fields to boost energy storage at low fields, surpassing single-layer and other lead-free ferroelectric thin films for eco-friendly electronics.

💡 This perspective introduces bonding chemistry as a unified, atom-level framework linking carbon structure to electrochemical behavior in rechargeable-ion batteries. It uniquely integrates C/C hybridization, carbon-heteroatom interactions, and dynamic ion-framework bonding, establishing bond-descriptor-based design principles that connect synthesis to storage thermodynamics, kinetics, and reversibility—enabling more systematic, predictive carbon framework engineering.

item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This review uniquely addresses air sensitivity and residual alkali in sodium-ion layered oxide cathodes, highlighting sodium-specific challenges absent in lithium-ion systems: NaHCO₃ formation, severe Na⁺/H⁺ exchange, and narrow processing windows. It bridges formation mechanisms, characterization, and modification strategies, offering future perspectives to guide practical, air-stable, high-performance cathode development.
